questions.question: Pressing F5 in PowerPoint starts the slide show from ___.
questions.explanation: F5 starts the slide show from the very first slide (beginning of the presentation). To start from the current slide, use Shift+F5.

questions.question: Pressing Shift+F5 in PowerPoint starts the slide show from ___.
questions.explanation: Shift+F5 starts the slide show from the currently selected (active) slide. F5 starts from the first slide.

questions.question: Which view in PowerPoint shows all slides as small thumbnails for rearranging?
questions.explanation: Slide Sorter View displays all slides as small thumbnails in a grid layout, making it easy to rearrange slides by dragging and dropping.

questions.question: A slide transition is applied between ___.
questions.explanation: A transition is a visual effect that occurs when moving from one slide to the next. It is applied between two slides, not to objects within a slide.

questions.question: An animation in PowerPoint is applied to ___.
questions.explanation: Animations are applied to individual objects (text boxes, images, shapes, charts) within a slide. Transitions are applied between slides.

questions.question: To print 3 slides per page with lines for notes, you should use ___.
questions.explanation: Handouts with 3 slides per page include three slide thumbnails on the left and ruled lines on the right for the audience to write notes. This is the most popular handout format.

questions.question: The file extension of a PowerPoint presentation is ___.
questions.explanation: PowerPoint presentations are saved with the .pptx extension. .docx is for Word, .xlsx is for Excel, and .pdf is a portable document format.

questions.question: Which PowerPoint view is the default editing view?
questions.explanation: Normal View is the default view in PowerPoint. It shows the slide panel on the left, the main editing area in the center, and the notes panel at the bottom.

questions.question: Which type of animation makes an object appear on the slide?
questions.explanation: Entrance animations make objects appear on the slide (e.g., Fly In, Fade, Zoom). Exit animations make objects disappear. Emphasis animations draw attention to objects already on the slide.

questions.question: The Slide Master is used to ___.
options: Apply uniform formatting to all slides
questions.explanation: The Slide Master controls the appearance (fonts, colors, backgrounds, logos) of all slides that use its layout. Changes to the Slide Master are automatically applied to all slides.

questions.question: A .ppsx file opens directly in ___ mode.
questions.explanation: A .ppsx (PowerPoint Show) file opens directly in Slide Show mode, showing the presentation full screen without the editing interface. A .pptx file opens in editing mode.

questions.question: What does pressing 'B' during a slide show do?
options: Goes back to the previous slide
questions.explanation: Pressing 'B' during a slide show turns the screen black (useful for pausing the presentation to talk without visual distraction). Press 'B' again to return to the slide. 'W' turns the screen white.

questions.question: SmartArt in PowerPoint is used to create ___.
questions.explanation: SmartArt provides pre-designed graphical layouts for presenting information visually, such as process flows, hierarchies, cycles, and lists.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut inserts a new slide in PowerPoint?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + M inserts a new slide in PowerPoint. Ctrl + N creates a new blank presentation, Ctrl + S saves, and Ctrl + D duplicates the selected slide.

questions.question: Kiosk mode in PowerPoint is used for ___.
questions.explanation: Kiosk mode (Set Up Show → Browsed at a kiosk) creates a self-running, full-screen presentation that loops continuously. The audience cannot manually advance slides — only automatic timings work.
